title: Approval decision tree and audit minification notes
content:
Purpose: sketch a lightweight approval decision-tree UX and a compact audit payload strategy for customer-managed networking changes. Goal is an operator-friendly flow that produces minimal verifiable evidence for compliance teams (SRE, SOC) while keeping payload size, retention, and cross-customer telemetry costs low.

Context and constraints
- Private deployments require customer-managed networks (VPCs, on-prem adapters). Changes to those networks must be authorized, auditable, and replayable for post-mortem.
- Customers care about: minimal data leakage (no long-lived raw configs), proof of who approved what and when, and the ability to reconstruct the decision chain within 30 days.
- Redwood needs compact, searchable artifacts that: (a) defend against tampering, (b) map to internal rollout/rollback actions, and (c) are easy to ingest into our Console and customer's SIEMs.

High-level approach (two orthogonal pieces)
1) Approval Decision Tree (operator UX + machine-checkable steps)
   - Node types: request, vet, approve, escalate, automated-check, rollback-trigger.
   - Each node emits a short event: {event_type, node_id, actor_id, timestamp, outcome_code, short_reason_code}. (We will stringify/encode event series; see payload minification section.)
   - Decision tree template per-change-type (e.g., firewall-rule-add, peering-update, route-table-modify). Templates define required nodes and optional branches (escalation thresholds).
   - UX: compact in-console flow with inline checklist items and a single-summary confirmation that is cryptographically associated with the change bundle.

2) Compact Audit Payload (minified, tamper-evident, verifiable)
   - Principle: keep raw config diff out of central logs. Only store minimal fingerprints, hashes, and human-readable labels. Full diffs live with the customer or in short-lived encrypted blobs.
   - Payload fields (minimal): [change_id, template_id, actor_ids (list short), timestamps (iso), final_outcome, evidence_refs (short ids), signature_bundle].
   - Evidence refs: pointers to artifacts (e.g., presigned encrypted blob in customer S3, or ephemeral service escrow token). Artifact pointers are short opaque ids (no raw content).
   - Signature bundle: signer public key id + signature over canonicalized payload (base64). Primary signer is operator who approved final node; automated nodes hold signed attestations from our service.

Design tradeoffs and questions
- Q: How do we support customers who demand full change diffs for audits? Proposal: provide an opt-in encrypted artifact escrow that the customer stores (in their own S3/GCS) and we include only the stable reference in Redwood logs.
- Q: Retention vs compliance: compliance teams sometimes need multi-year records. We should support export hooks (signed archives) but default retention in Console logs is short (90 days) to reduce cost.
- Q: How to balance quick rollback vs proof? Keep rollback triggers minimal in logs but store rollback-safety-check signatures that are verifiable.

Example: flow for a firewall rule addition (text only sketch)
- change_id: CHG-20251112-374
- template_id: firewall-rule-add-v1
- events (minified):
  - E1: request|n1|actor:net-ops-12|ts:2025-11-12T11:54:03Z|out:pending|rc:REQ
  - E2: automated-check|n2|actor:svc-fw-lint|ts:2025-11-12T11:54:10Z|out:pass|rc:LINT_OK
  - E3: vet|n3|actor:sec-review-3|ts:2025-11-12T12:01:04Z|out:escalate|rc:PORT_RANGE
  - E4: approve|n4|actor:eng-lead-4|ts:2025-11-12T12:15:20Z|out:accept|rc:APPROVED
- final_payload (what we persist in central audit index): change_id, template_id, actors:[net-ops-12,svc-fw-lint,sec-review-3,eng-lead-4], started:2025-11-12T11:54:03Z, ended:2025-11-12T12:15:20Z, outcome:approved, evidence_refs:[EVID-7f2a], sigs:[sig-v2-abc]

Storage / telemetry considerations
- Indexable fields for Console search: change_id, template_id, final_outcome, actor_ids (short), start/end timestamps, evidence_refs. All human-readable metadata must be short strings.
- Avoid storing raw IP ranges, full route tables, firewall payloads. Where necessary use hashed fingerprints (sha256 prefix) plus optional encrypted escrow.
- Compress series of events into a compact binary protobuf for internal transport; strip to the minified JSON for Console ingestion.

Operator UX sketches (notes)
- Compact checklist view: single-line timeline for the change with colored state chips. Clicking the chip expands the minified event (actor, time, short reason).
- Approval modal: free-text justification allowed but stored as ephemeral (display-only) in console; an admin can request export which generates an encrypted bundle with that free text included.
- Escalation notices: inline suggestions ("route to security lead") with a one-click escalate that attaches the minimal reason code.

Security and tamper-resistance
- Every final_payload persisted must carry a signature. Signatures are rotated per-window and anchored in a rotation log to make replay attacks harder.
- The Console shows a small "proof" badge that can be expanded to reveal signature/public-key metadata and a verification helper.

Example minimal verification checklist for auditors
- Does final_payload include change_id, template_id, actor list, start/end, outcome, evidence_refs, signatures?
- Can signatures be resolved to a known key id in rotation log? (link provided)
- Are evidence_refs resolvable to an encrypted blob stored with customer or escrow?

Open engineering TODOs (rough priorities)
- [P0] Define canonical payload schema for final_payload and event minification. (owner: Marco Ruiz, JIRA PD-981)
- [P0] Implement signature bundle format + rotation plan. (owner: Liam O'Connor)
- [P1] UX prototype for compact checklist and proof modal in Console. (owner: Aisha Patel)
- [P2] Escrow integration options: customer-S3 presigned vs Redwood ephemeral enclave.
- [P3] Export tool for long-term retention (signed archive generation).

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: Customers misinterpret minified payloads as insufficient evidence. Mitigation: provide clear docs and optional full-escrow exports; include example legal language.
- Risk: Signatures/key rotation complexity leaks into customer audits. Mitigation: simple verification helper in Console and well-documented rotation schedule.

Notes / rough links to related work
- See CON-1723 for attestation key management notes.
- See design sketch in github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/ (branch: approval-protos) for proto shapes (proto sketches only, not final).

Unresolved questions we should discuss in next product sync
- Retention SLAs for different customer tiers (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Default 90d ok? Enterprise opt-in for 3y exports?
- Escrow model: default to customer-managed buckets to minimize Redwood liability? Or offer managed escrow as opt-in paid feature?
- Should automated-check artifacts be stored longer than manual approvals? (Weigh cost vs forensic value.)

Quick annex: proposed short codes (examples to standardize)
- REQ = request submitted
- LINT_OK = automated lint passed
- PORT_RANGE = requires escalation due to non-standard ports
- APPROVED = final approval
- ROLLBACK_TRIG = rollback executed

Bottom line: aim for a system that is operator-friendly, compact by default, auditable on demand. Next steps: finalize payload schema (PD-981), prototype signature scheme, and ship a Console proof-of-concept so customers and compliance teams can validate assumptions.
